Basic terms

What do these words mean?

Start with these terms

TermPlain meaning
Token addressThe full address identifying the token on its chain. Names and symbols can be copied.
Dev or creatorThe person or team launching the token. Check which wallets and permissions belong to them.
WalletAn account that can hold assets. One person can use several wallets.
SupplyThe number of token units. Total issued units, locked units, pool reserves, and units holders can transfer answer different questions.
AllocationTokens assigned to someone at launch, such as a team or treasury. Record whether they paid for them.
Cost basisWhat someone paid to acquire their tokens, using a stated accounting method. Missing purchase history means the cost is unknown.
BundleTransactions submitted together for ordered execution. A scanner may also use this word for launch purchases it detects as coordinated. Check its definition.
Linked walletsWallets with evidence connecting them. Record confirmed links and suspected links separately.
Liquidity poolAssets held for trading. The pool's reserves and rules affect how much a sale receives.
Price impactHow much your trade changes the quoted price. A large sale can receive much less per token than a small one.
Permission or authorityA right to change something, such as minting more units or freezing accounts.
Vesting and unlockA schedule releasing tokens over time, and the point when units become available.
Creator feeA share of eligible trading fees paid or accrued to a creator under the platform's rules.
DumpingSelling a large amount quickly enough to put heavy pressure on the market.

How to investigate it

Copy the full token address and chain first. Open its explorer page. Identify the creator wallet, ordinary holders, pool accounts, supply, and permissions. Save the links and check time. If a field is unclear, write down the provider's definition before using the number.

Practical case — illustrative

SAMPLE is a made-up token used throughout this course. It has 150m issued units: 30m in pool reserves, 20m locked for the team, and 100m available to ordinary holders. A wallet with 2m holds about 1.3% of total issued units, or 2% of available holder units. Always say which total you use.

The examples show snapshots at different times. The course is arranged by topic; check each timestamp before comparing balances.

Keep this record

Record the token address, chain, check time, address roles, and the meaning of each supply number.

Add these findings to your review worksheet →

Check your understanding — answered

Two tokens have the same name. Which one am I checking? Match the full token address and chain.

The holder percentage differs between tools. What should I check? Check their supply definitions, snapshot times, and coverage.

Is every large holder the dev? Identify its role and look for ownership evidence. It may be a pool, exchange, or unrelated holder.

SAMPLE is made up for this course. Date each finding. For a real token, use current transaction records and platform rules. Inspect shows sampled trades; use external records to check ownership and permissions.
